messages:
aya: quick design check — thinking about the API keys table. two quick problems: permission labels are hard to scan, and the primary CTA sequence (create -> copy -> revoke) feels noisy on small screens. attaching mock: https://figma.com/file/xyz (mock 3)
mike: saw the mock. agree re: scanability. suggestion: show compact 'scope chips' with a tooltip for full list. chips would allow a single-row layout instead of multi-line perms.
sam: compact chips sound good, but we need to ensure keyboard focus order. if chips are interactive we should make them non-focusable and only the row-level disclosure focusable.
nora: accessibility nit: if chips are not focusable they still need descriptive text for screen readers. consider aria-describedby on the row or an offscreen summary like "Scopes: read, write, deploy".
kim: also we should think about copy for 'Create API key' modal. current copy: "This key will be shown once." suggestion: "This key will be revealed once. Be sure to store it securely — you won't be able to view it again." (short but explicit)
aya: love that copy tweak. another UX question: where to surface 'least privilege' warning? currently buried in the modal footer. proposal: a small inline hint next to scope selector with a subtle warning icon.
mike: inline hint is better for discoverability. design note: use subtle amber color + :warning: icon. avoid modal-scrolling if the policy text grows.
sam: front-end constraints: we need to keep modal height stable. we can collapse long policy text behind "learn more" accordion. basic warning should be max one line.
nora: copy suggestion for screen reader: the warning icon needs aria-hidden=true and the text should be read normally. also ensure the modal's initial focus lands on the close or primary CTA depending on the flow.
aya: question for product: should the post-create experience show a persistent row with an expiration countdown for ephemeral keys? currently we show a toast only.
kim: engineering prefers showing ephemeral keys inline with an expiry pill (e.g., "expires in 1h") so users can revoke early. toast-only is bad for discoverability.
mike: visual: expiry pill on the left, then name, then scopes chips, then actions (copy, reveal, revoke). On mobile actions collapse into kebab menu.
sam: mobile collapsed kebab needs clear affordances: 'Copy' and 'Revoke' first, 'Details' last. also ensure swipe-to-delete is disabled for security.
nora: accessibility: for 'Reveal API key' button we need an aria-label that includes duration and danger: e.g., `aria-label="Reveal API key. Visible for 30 seconds."` — also consider a polite screen-reader announcement when the key is revealed.
aya: leaving a small copy item: when key is revealed, microcopy should say "Visible for 30s — copy now or it will be hidden." and maybe show a progress ring.
kim: implementation note: backend can send an expiration TTL; front-end should gate the reveal action behind a short auth check if session is older than X mins.
mike: tiny UI nit: the revoke confirmation pattern currently uses a destructive modal with a single 'Revoke' button and a cancel. request we add a short reason dropdown in the modal so SRE can triage revoked keys.
sam: reason dropdown is fine but make it optional. also add an audit log entry skeleton so the backend can store revocation_reason.
nora: audit log event should include a screen-reader friendly summary when viewing the revocation in the Admin timeline.
aya: final asks for design: 1) provide two visual variants (chips vs single-line summary) for an A/B test, 2) update modal copy as suggested, 3) add aria-label examples to the spec, 4) show ephemeral pill design, 5) include revocation reason field mock.
mike: will push two variants to figma and annotate states. planning to prototype keyboard nav and mobile collapse.
sam: I'll add the aria attributes and keyboard behavior to the component PR. linking draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/front-end/pull/987
kim: I'll stub backend TTL + audit log fields in the key-service spec. will add a feature flag for ephemeral inline display.
deploy-bot: reminder: staging deploy scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC — include feature-flagged key-ui changes in the deploy checklist.
aya: thanks all. I'll collect these and update the product ticket with acceptance criteria by EOD. :thumbsup:
